newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - July 24.

text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Thursday, as reported by Kyodo news agency.
-- Health and Welfare Ministry eyes replacing standard medicine price system with upper limit on prices paid by health insurance system.
-- European Commission OK's planned merger between U.S. aircraft makers Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp.
-- Panel on investment and loan programme calls for stopping state loans to JNR Settlement Corp and forest business in year starting April 1998.
-- Fair Trade Commission (FTC) sees no proof of Anti-Monopoly Law violation in Japan's photo colour film and paper markets.
-- Tight fiscal budget for 1998/99 may force Construction Ministry to drop some 10 dam construction projects.
-- Government to accept North Korea's plan to allow 15 to 20 Japanese women, married to North Koreans, to visit relatives in Japan next month.
-- Tokyo prosecutors likely to indict Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) for alleged violation of banking law in corporate racketeer payoff scandal.
